properties.name: saga-forge.transport.workers
properties.description: Delivery threads of the in-memory transport; messages with the same ordering key (aggregate) always use the same one.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.max-attempts
properties.description: Failed deliveries of a message before it is set aside for an operator.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.initial-backoff
properties.description: Wait after a message's first failed delivery; doubled per further failure.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.max-backoff
properties.description: Longest wait between delivery attempts of a message.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.lease-duration
properties.description: How long a leased message is reserved for this application instance before another may take it.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.poll-interval
properties.description: Longest wait between polls of the message store when nothing signals new messages.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.retention
properties.description: How long consumed messages are kept in the message store.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.retention-sweep-interval
properties.description: How often consumed messages older than the retention are removed.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.heartbeat-interval
properties.description: How often this application instance refreshes its heartbeat in the message store.

properties.name: saga-forge.transport.modulith-interop
properties.description: Whether the transport stores its messages in Spring Modulith's event publication registry when it is present, so the application has one outbox.

values.description: Never create tables; missing tables fail startup. For Flyway or Liquibase users.
Create Saga Forge's tables from schema.sql when none exist; never alters existing tables.
Publish every recorded domain event through Spring's ApplicationEventPublisher inside the unit of work's transaction (Spring Modulith listeners).
Publish an event as an application event when the transport delivers it, after the recording transaction committed.
Do not publish recorded domain events as application events.
